prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map depicts an indoor retail space with a ceiling above, large background windows roughly 3–5 metres behind the foreground, a clothing rack on the left, a short white display stand on the right, and a person wearing a cap, glasses, and fur-trimmed collar in the centre. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer approaches this person from roughly 2–2.5 metres away in frames 1–2 to about 1–1.5 metres in frame 3 and within arm's reach (0.4–0.6 metres) in frames 4–5, while the person turns from facing and looking toward the camera wearer in frames 1–2 to facing forward-right and looking down at a handheld smartphone within his own arm's reach in frames 3–5. In frames 1 and 5, the camera wearer holds a second smartphone within arm's reach (about 0.2–0.3 metres away) at the bottom centre, which appears brightest white and partially occludes the other person's lower torso, while everyone's lower bodies and the rack's base are cropped below the bottom edge. The depth map clearly separates the depth planes between the camera wearer's near phone, the mid-ground person, the flanking clothing rack and display stand (about 1–1.5 metres behind/beside the person), and the distant window wall in a way that is harder to gauge quantitatively from RGB alone. However, the map is unreliable on the glass windows (where outdoor trees and reflections flatten into uniform dark regions) and in frames 1–2 where a bright artifact appears along the right border wall.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates foreground silhouettes against the unlabelled background room, tracking the central person as his mask expands from the lower-left/centre at roughly 2–2.5 metres away in frames 1–2 to fill most of the frame at 0.4–0.6 metres in frames 4–5 as the camera wearer approaches and the person turns right to look down at his phone. In frame 1, the camera wearer's smartphone held at 0.2–0.3 metres in the lower-centre foreground is segmented as 'cell phone' directly in front of and partially occluding the standing person, and in frame 4 the other person's handheld phone is segmented as 'cell phone' at the bottom-right edge within both people's arm's reach. Compared to RGB, the masks sharply delineate the outer contour of the person's headwear and shoulders against the cluttered window Mullions, while also highlighting the on-screen selfie reflection inside the camera wearer's phone in frame 1 as a separate 'person' mask. However, the map is unreliable for scene layout and object identity: it leaves the ceiling, windows, and the camera wearer's phone in frame 5 completely unsegmented, and it severely misclassifies background and handheld objects—labelling a background reflection as 'umbrella' (frame 2), the left clothing rack at 1.5–2.5 metres as 'suitcase' (frame 3) and 'motorcycle' (frame 5), the right display stand at 2 metres as 'refrigerator' (frame 3), and the person's phone in frame 5 as 'remote'. Additionally, the person's furry collar and the camera wearer's occluding phone create large unsegmented black holes inside the person's torso mask in frames 4 and 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D body keypoints (yellow) and hand skeletons (magenta) on a black background for the single visible person standing in front of the camera wearer, with no background layout or objects represented. In frames 1 and 2, when the person is roughly 2–2.5 metres away and cropped below the chest, a symmetric cluster of facial keypoints and a horizontal shoulder bar show his head and torso facing directly toward and looking at the camera wearer, with his right elbow extending downward in frame 2 as his arms remain mostly out of view below the frame edge. By frame 3, at roughly 1–1.5 metres distance, the shoulder-to-hip torso box shifts into an angled profile and both arms bend forward into densely articulated magenta hand skeletons positioned just in front of his chest, showing him turned slightly right, looking downward, and holding an object with both hands within his arm's reach. This skeletal wireframe makes the exact joint locations of the occluded torso, the elbow bend, and the overlapping finger poses in frame 3 much easier to parse than in the dark, low-contrast clothing of the RGB image. However, the pose map is completely unreliable at close range (0.4–0.6 metres in frames 4 and 5), where heavy cropping of the lower body and self-occlusion from the side-profile posture cause the detector to miss all body and hand keypoints entirely, and it also fails to detect the camera wearer's own hand holding the foreground phone in frames 1 and 5.
